one_liner: Jira Cloud has a broad REST v3 API with self-serve OAuth 2.0 (3LO) and basic/API-token auth, plus an official Atlassian Rovo MCP server.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 (3LO) apps are registered self-serve in the developer console. Ad-hoc scripts use basic auth (email:API token). Connect apps use JWT. Forge is the app platform.
access_notes: Draft sources say REST API access is free on all Jira plans, including Free. Atlassian's own pages show the developer console is self-serve for creating OAuth apps. No page shows paid-only access. Points-based rate limits apply to apps.
blocker_notes: Tier 2 per-tenant rate limits require review, but apps start in Tier 1 and this does not block building a toolkit.

evidence.quote: Access to the REST APIs is free for all Jira plans.
In the Developer console, select the **Create** dropdown and choose **OAuth 2.0 integration** to create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
For integrations that are not Forge or Connect apps, use OAuth 2.0 authorization code grants (3LO) for security
For personal scripts, bots, and ad-hoc execution of the REST APIs use basic authentication.
For Connect apps, authentication (JWT-based) is built into the Connect libraries.
The Jira REST API enables you to interact with Jira programmatically.
Build a secure, scalable bridge between Atlassian and external AI solutions.
consider using Atlassian Rovo MCP as an alternative to direct API queries
